note: The fuzz harness always enables PROXY parsing, so inputs starting with a PROXY header are delivered directly to the vulnerable parser.
The harness only forwards inputs that already contain a complete request terminator, so the payload must include both a PROXY header and a valid HTTP request tail.
The first bytes are reinterpreted as a PROXY protocol frame before HTTP parsing occurs.
The parser reads the attacker-chosen version, family, and length fields directly from the input buffer.

code: size = proto_signature_length + (unsigned int)ntohs(hdr->len); if (size > sizeof(*hdr)) return NULL;
note: The fixed-size check admits only small lengths, so the interesting cases are the smallest legal TCP4/TCP6 frames that still shift the HTTP parser state.
After a minimal valid frame is accepted, parsing continues from the first HTTP byte following the PROXY block.
The remaining-region scan uses the shifted pointer and adjusted size; a malformed frame length can make this scan observe bytes outside the intended HTTP request area.
